reasoning: Cantilever with tip load: M = PL = 300,000 N·mm; stress = 6PL/(b h^2); deflection = 4PL^3/(E b h^3). Checks use P = 2200 N and h - 0.5 mm (REQ-006). Allowables: yield/1.25 and ultimate/1.4 per material. Al 6061 governs at yield ~220.8 MPa, and Ti and Steel are limited by deflection (Ti) or yield (Steel). Best candidates: Al h=25, b=15 mm (~375 mm2, ~1.01 kg/m); Ti h=20, b=12 mm (~235 mm2, ~1.04 kg/m); Steel h=20, b=15 mm (~300 mm2, ~2.36 kg/m). Al is the lightest, with Ti very close. Stock thickness and aspect ratio (REQ-005, REQ-007) are checked for each.

notes.Al 6061-T6: Yield allowable is 276/1.25 = 220.8 MPa, so at 2200 N and 0.5 mm thinner, the stress requirement needs b*h'^2 >= 8968 mm^3 and the deflection requirement needs b*h'^3 >= 143,700 mm^4; search h = 25 mm (h' = 24.5) with b about 15 mm (h/b = 1.67 <= 2), giving about 375 mm^2 and 1.01 kg/m with MS near 0 and tip deflection about 1.95 mm.
notes.Ti-6Al-4V: Ti's stress limits (704 and 679 MPa) are loose, so deflection governs with E = 113.8 GPa and b*h'^3 >= 87,000 mm^4; search h = 20 mm (h' = 19.5) with b about 11.8 mm (h/b = 1.7 <= 2), giving about 235 mm^2 and 1.04 kg/m, which is close to Al but not lighter.
notes.Steel 4130: Yield allowable is 435/1.25 = 348 MPa, and the stiffer E = 205 GPa makes deflection easy, so yield requires b*h'^2 >= 5690 mm^3; search h = 20 mm with b about 15 mm (h/b = 1.33), giving about 300 mm^2 and 2.36 kg/m, which is roughly twice the mass of Al or Ti.

attacks.title: REQ-006 case: load +10% and plate 0.5 mm thinner
attacks.rationale: Load 2200 N and thickness 24.5 mm. Survives, but yield margin is only +0.004 and ultimate +0.007, so the requirement passes by a hair. Tip deflection 1.95 mm is within limit.

attacks.title: Machining error: thickness 2 mm under (25 to 23 mm)
attacks.rationale: Stress and stiffness both scale with thickness squared or cubed. Yield margin drops to -0.027 and ultimate to -0.024, and deflection rises to 2.15 mm. A realistic machining error breaks REQ-001 and REQ-002.

attacks.title: Width loss: 2 mm under (15 to 13 mm)
attacks.rationale: Width enters stress and stiffness linearly, but there is no margin left. Yield margin is -0.003 and ultimate is about 0. A 13% loss in width fails strength at the nominal load.

attacks.title: Layout change: arm 15 mm longer (150 to 165 mm)
attacks.rationale: Moment rises 10%, so stress rises to about 211 MPa. Margins fall from +0.15 to +0.045 (yield) and +0.048 (ultimate). Deflection rises to 2.23 mm. Still passes, but a small layout change eats most of the remaining margin.

attacks.title: Combined realistic errors: load +25%, thickness -1 mm, width -1 mm, arm +10 mm
attacks.rationale: Load 2500 N, arm 160 mm, section 14 x 24 mm. Stress about 298 MPa, yield margin -0.258, ultimate -0.256, tip deflection 3.07 mm (over the 3 mm limit). Stacked realistic errors break strength and stiffness together.

rationale: G-01 is blocking: the Monte Carlo probability of failure is 1.90% against a 1% limit, with 5% of parts below a +0.030 governing margin, and the team's 15 x 25 mm Al 6061-T6 has only about +0.004 yield margin at REQ-006 (load +10%, plate -0.5 mm) and collapses under the red-team combined case (load +25%, thickness -1 mm, width -1 mm, arm +10 mm). Widening the section adds bending stiffness with no change to the stock thickness, so the design can be fixed in another round.
directive: Increase the width from 15 mm to 22 mm, keeping the 25 mm stock thickness (25/22 = 1.14, which satisfies REQ-007). Re-run the physics check with the REQ-006 case and the G-04 combined case (load +25%, thickness 24 mm, width 21 mm, arm 160 mm), and aim for a worst-case yield margin of at least +0.03 at factor 1.25; the hand estimate for 22 x 25 mm is about +0.11 in that combined case, and tip deflection stays well under 3 mm.

reasoning: Directive applied: width 22 mm, thickness 25 mm (25/22 = 1.14, passes REQ-007; both dimensions are in REQ-004 ranges and 25 mm is stock per REQ-005). Hand checks, with M = P x L and sigma = 6M/(b t^2): base case 2000 N, 150 mm, 22x25 gives sigma about 131 MPa and Al 6061-T6 yield MS about +0.69. REQ-006 case (2200 N, 24.5 mm, 22 mm wide) gives sigma about 150 MPa, yield MS about +0.47, ultimate MS about +0.48, and deflection about 1.3 mm. G-04 as literally specified (2500 N, 21 mm wide, 24 mm thick, 160 mm arm) gives sigma about 198 MPa and Al yield MS of +0.11 at factor 1.25, which is the +0.11 figure. That is the worst case and clears the +0.03 target. The 22x25 section with the G-04 load and arm would give about +0.27. Deflection in G-04 is about 2.05 mm, under 3 mm. Al 6061-T6 has the lowest density, so it gives the lowest mass among materials that pass. Ti and steel are checked for comparison only, since they are heavier.

notes.Al 6061-T6: Search the directed 22 mm x 25 mm section and confirm the G-04 worst case (21x24, 2500 N, 160 mm arm) gives yield MS of about +0.11 at factor 1.25, above the +0.03 target, with ultimate MS and deflection under 3 mm also checked. Al is the lightest candidate, so if it passes it is the lowest-mass choice.
notes.Ti-6Al-4V: Run the directed 22x25 section and the G-04 case as a comparison only; yield MS should be well above +0.03 (about +2.5 in G-04) because of the 880 MPa yield, but density 4430 kg/m3 is about 1.6 times Al, so it is not the lowest-mass option. Keep thickness at 25 mm stock and check REQ-006 for completeness.
notes.Steel 4130: Run the directed 22x25 section and the G-04 case as a comparison only; steel passes yield with margin (about +0.75 in G-04 at factor 1.25) but density 7850 kg/m3 makes it about 2.9 times Al's mass for the same section, so it is a backup. Confirm REQ-006 and the deflection limit and report only if Al fails.

summary: All six structural rules (S-01 to S-06) pass, with yield, ultimate, and worst-case margins of +0.85, +0.78, and +0.60, and tip deflection of 2.51 mm. Open items are the M-01 typical allowables, M-05 dissimilar-metal joint, X-01 and X-02 fracture and fatigue work, and the P-01 to P-03 procurement requirements, while P-04 export control is informational only.
top_risks: X-02: Fatigue is not analyzed, and no cyclic load cases such as launch vibration have been evaluated.
M-01: Design margins rest on typical handbook values rather than MMPDS A- or B-basis allowables for this alloy, temper, and thickness.
P-01: The specialty metal (DFARS 252.225-7009) melt origin must be confirmed as US or a qualifying country before purchase.
